subject: [hw] opus-hevcdec: HEVC decode page list = DEC02's H.264 list + 0x15000 (LAT HEVC_VLD); 17.7% of HEVC ops need VDEC_ALL
body: Measured on the host (phone vpud + vendor libs, 12-AU 320x240 and 6-AU 1080p HEVC, all frames completed): touched pages of 0x16000000: 0x00000, 0x02000 (WRAP_TOP +0x004 R, +0x01c W), 0x04000, 0x0d000 (+0x00c only), 0x0f000, 0x10000, 0x11000 incl. 0x11800-0x11bff (LAT_VLD_TOP / UBE regs 0x11a30, 0x11aac, 0x11b98), 0x15000 (LAT HEVC_VLD, R+W, 59 distinct words), 0x16000 (+0xcac only), 0x20000, 0x21000, 0x23000, 0x24000, 0x25000, 0x28000 (HEVC_VLD, inside the frozen MISC window), 0x2e000 (+0x00c only), 0x2f000. No 0x12000/0x13000 (AVC only), nothing >= 0x30000. 2387 of 13487 accesses (17.7%) fall outside the ten frozen windows, so HEVC is impossible without RWVC_WIN_VDEC_ALL; the DEC07 page->domain rule (VDE < 0x20000, VDE2 >= 0x20000) and the larb {5,4} +0x00c allow-list are sufficient. HEVC video decode uses no GCE (0 flushes), same IRQs as H.264 (SPI 425 then 424 per frame). Details: facts/HEVC_DEC_PROTOCOL.md section 4. No kernel change beyond rev 3 is needed for HEVC video.
